detail.body:
# Description

`general_gemm()` rejects compact, unswizzled MXFP8 scales: a 64×64 tensor with rowwise scales `(64, 2)` or columnwise scales `(2, 64)` fails during GEMM preparation because the swizzle API requires padded storage. Accept exact logical scale shapes and write them directly into padded, swizzled output, filling padding with zeros. Apply this to both single GEMM and list-based `general_grouped_gemm()` preparation while preserving the caller's buffers and unswizzled flag.

Fixes #3518.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Changes

- Accept exact compact MXFP8 scale shapes at the checked swizzle boundary. Other consumers retain their existing scale-shape validation.
- Fuse padding into a bounds-checked swizzle kernel, without an intermediate padding allocation or copy. Use a flat CUDA grid so tall scale planes do not hit the 65,535-block limit of a grid's second dimension.
- Batch up to 32 compact tensors per launch. Mixed batches retain the existing optimized kernels for padded tensors.
- Allocate padded destination shapes and correct shared-buffer offsets in the single- and multi-tensor PyTorch helpers.
- Document the C API contract and add common C API and full-binding PyTorch regressions for both orientations, single/grouped GEMM, compact/padded/mixed storage, exact output bytes, input preservation, large batches, tall shapes, and invalid inputs.

The separate `GroupedTensor` API and unchecked attention swizzle contract are unchanged. GEMM regression operands are copied from independently quantized reference planes to isolate swizzle/GEMM behavior. The separate rectangular compact in-place quantization mismatch noted during investigation is outside this fix.

## Validation

Built the complete common library and PyTorch extension from this source on NVIDIA GB300 (compute capability 10.3), targeting `103a`. Verified the loaded Python package, PyTorch extension, and common library all resolve to the checkout. Environment: CUDA 13.4, driver 580.178.04, PyTorch `2.14.0a0+b2c75dd062.nv26.09`, cuDNN 9.26.0, NCCL 2.31.2, Python 3.12.3, pytest 9.1.1. Optional NCCL EP and CuTeDSL components were disabled for this build.

- All 26 cases in `tests/pytorch/mxfp8/test_compact_scales_gemm.py` passed with `NVTE_MXFP8_PER_TILE_SWIZZLE=0` and again with `=1`: 18 numerical single/grouped GEMM cases covering TN/NN/NT and 8 byte-layout cases.
- The same 26 cases passed under Compute Sanitizer memcheck with zero errors.
- The original 64×64 `quantize_()` → GEMM reproducer passed for compact TN and NN, as did padded TN and NN controls, each in a fresh process.
- All 10 new C API cases in `tests/cpp/operator/test_compact_swizzle.cu` passed against the complete common library in both swizzle modes; both modes also passed memcheck with zero errors.
- All 15 existing `test_mxfp8_quantize_swizzle_fusion.py` cases passed. None of the final focused tests were skipped.
- Earlier RTX A6000 checks covered both common swizzle modes, exact bytes through the real PyTorch allocation helpers, and CUDA graph replay. Four positive compact-input common regressions failed on unmodified `swizzle.cu`, as expected.
- Repository pre-commit checks, focused cpplint, license checks, Python compilation, and whitespace checks passed.

Full L0 suites and JAX tests were not run. No performance claim is made for this implementation.

# Checklist

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing focused unit tests pass locally with my changes

Draft pending author review before maintainer review.

files.patch:
@@ -41,6 +41,7 @@ add_executable(test_operator

                test_causal_softmax.cu
                test_swizzle.cu
+               test_compact_swizzle.cu
                test_multi_swizzle.cu
                test_swap_first_dims.cu
                test_grouped_gemm.cu

@@ -0,0 +1,173 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2022-2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+
+"""Compact MXFP8 scales are padded as part of GEMM preparation."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from mxfp8_utils import swizzle_mxfp8_scale
+
+import transformer_engine.pytorch as te
+import transformer_engine_torch as tex
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.cpp_extensions import general_gemm, general_grouped_gemm
+from transformer_engine.pytorch.tensor.mxfp8_tensor import MXFP8Quantizer, MXFP8Tensor
+
+
+def _copy_with_scale_layout(reference, compact):
+    """Copy independently quantized planes, isolating swizzle from quantization."""
+    rows, cols = reference.shape
+    row_scales = reference._rowwise_scale_inv
+    col_scales = reference._columnwise_scale_inv
+    if compact:
+        row_scales = row_scales[:rows, : cols // 32]
+        col_scales = col_scales[: rows // 32, :cols]
+    return MXFP8Tensor(
+        shape=reference.shape,
+        dtype=reference.dtype,
+        device=reference.device,
+        rowwise_data=reference._rowwise_data.clone(),
+        columnwise_data=reference._columnwise_data.clone(),
+        rowwise_scale_inv=row_scales.clone().contiguous(),
+        columnwise_scale_inv=col_scales.clone().contiguous(),
+        fp8_dtype=tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3,
+        quantizer=MXFP8Quantizer(tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3),
+        with_gemm_swizzled_scales=False,
+    )
+
+
+def _snapshot(tensor):
+    return [
+        (plane.data_ptr(), plane.clone())
+        for plane in (
+            tensor._rowwise_data,
+            tensor._columnwise_data,
+            tensor._rowwise_scale_inv,
+            tensor._columnwise_scale_inv,
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def _check_unchanged(tensor, snapshot):
+    assert not tensor._with_gemm_swizzled_scales
+    for plane, (pointer, before) in zip(
+        (
+            tensor._rowwise_data,
+            tensor._columnwise_data,
+            tensor._rowwise_scale_inv,
+            tensor._columnwise_scale_inv,
+        ),
+        snapshot,
+    ):
+        assert plane.data_ptr() == pointer
+        torch.testing.assert_close(plane, before, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not te.is_mxfp8_available(), reason="MXFP8 GEMM requires Blackwell")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["TN", "NN", "NT"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grouped", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("storage", ["compact", "padded", "mixed"])
+def test_compact_scales_gemm(layout, grouped, storage):
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    quantizer = MXFP8Quantizer(tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3)
+    operands_a, operands_b, expected = [], [], []
+    references_a, references_b = [], []
+    for i, shape in enumerate([(64, 64), (96, 160), (256, 128)]):
+        rows, cols = shape
+        b_shape = (96, cols) if layout == "TN" else (96, rows) if layout == "NN" else (rows, 96)
+        references = [quantizer(torch.randn(s, device="cuda")) for s in (shape, b_shape)]
+        references_a.append(references[0])
+        references_b.append(references[1])
+        operands_a.append(_copy_with_scale_layout(references[0], storage != "padded"))
+        operands_b.append(
+            _copy_with_scale_layout(
+                references[1], storage == "compact" or (storage == "mixed" and i % 2 == 0)
+            )
+        )
+        expected.append(general_gemm(*references, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16, layout=layout)[0])
+    operands = operands_a + operands_b
+    snapshots = [_snapshot(tensor) for tensor in operands]
+    if grouped:
+        actual = [torch.empty_like(tensor) for tensor in expected]
+        m_splits = [tensor.shape[0] for tensor in expected]
+        general_grouped_gemm(
+            references_a,
+            references_b,
+            expected,
+            [None] * len(expected),
+            torch.bfloat16,
+            layout=layout,
+            m_splits=m_splits,
+        )
+        general_grouped_gemm(
+            operands_a,
+            operands_b,
+            actual,
+            [None] * len(actual),
+            torch.bfloat16,
+            layout=layout,
+            m_splits=m_splits,
+        )
+    else:
+        actual = [
+            general_gemm(a, b, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16, layout=layout)[0]
+            for a, b in zip(operands_a, operands_b)
+        ]
+    for result, reference in zip(actual, expected):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    for tensor, snapshot in zip(operands, snapshots):
+        _check_unchanged(tensor, snapshot)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Scale swizzling requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rowwise", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grouped", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("per_tile", [False, True])
+def test_compact_scale_swizzle_bytes(rowwise, grouped, per_tile, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_MXFP8_PER_TILE_SWIZZLE", str(int(per_tile)))
+    shapes = [(32, 32), (64, 64), (96, 160), (128, 128), (160, 96), (4096, 4128)]
+    if grouped:
+        shapes = shapes * 12  # Cross the compact kernel's batch size.
+    tensors, expected, inputs = [], [], []
+    for i, (rows, cols) in enumerate(shapes):
+        padded_rows, padded_cols = (rows + 127) // 128 * 128, (cols + 127) // 128 * 128
+        scale_shape = (rows, cols // 32) if rowwise else (rows // 32, cols)
+        padded_shape = (
+            (padded_rows, padded_cols // 32) if rowwise else (padded_rows // 32, padded_cols)
+        )
+        scales = torch.randint(0, 256, scale_shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        padded = torch.zeros(padded_shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        padded[: scale_shape[0], : scale_shape[1]].copy_(scales)
+        expected.append(
+            swizzle_mxfp8_scale(padded_rows, padded_cols, padded, columnwise=not rowwise)
+        )
+        if grouped and i % 3 == 0:
+            scales = padded  # Exercise mixed compact/padded batches.
+        inputs.append((scales, scales.clone()))
+        data = torch.empty((rows, cols), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        tensors.append(
+            MXFP8Tensor(
+                shape=(rows, cols),
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                device="cuda",
+                rowwise_data=data if rowwise else None,
+                columnwise_data=None if rowwise else data,
+                rowwise_scale_inv=scales if rowwise else None,
+                columnwise_scale_inv=None if rowwise else scales,
+                fp8_dtype=tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3,
+                quantizer=MXFP8Quantizer(
+                    tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3, rowwise=rowwise, columnwise=not rowwise
+                ),
+                with_gemm_swizzled_scales=False,
+            )
+        )
+    if grouped:
+        tex.multi_tensor_swizzle_scales_for_gemm_(tensors, rowwise, not rowwise)
+    else:
+        for tensor in tensors:
+            tex.swizzle_scales_for_gemm_(tensor)
+    for tensor, reference, (scales, before) in zip(tensors, expected, inputs):
+        actual = tensor._rowwise_scale_inv if rowwise else tensor._columnwise_scale_inv
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(scales, before, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        # The multi-tensor helper updates one direction; its caller owns this flag.
+        assert tensor._with_gemm_swizzled_scales == (not grouped)

@@ -25,7 +25,10 @@ extern "C" {
  *
  *  Requirements:
  *  - scale_inv is stored in row-major.
- *  - scale_inv size is padded to 128x4 for row-scale and 4x128 for col-scale.
+ *  - Output scale_inv size is padded to 128x4 for row-scale and 4x128 for col-scale.
+ *  - MXFP8 inputs may instead use their exact logical scale shapes (M, ceil(K/32))
+ *    rowwise or (ceil(M/32), K) columnwise. Swizzling fills output padding with zeros.
+ *    Other input formats must be padded.
  *  - data is quantized along K-dimension, i.e. 1D-scaling block lies along the K-dimension.
  */
 void nvte_swizzle_scaling_factors(const NVTETensor input, NVTETensor output, cudaStream_t stream);
@@ -39,7 +42,10 @@ void nvte_swizzle_scaling_factors(const NVTETensor input, NVTETensor output, cud
  *
  *  Requirements:
  *  - scale_inv is stored in row-major.
- *  - scale_inv size is padded to 128x4 for row-scale and 4x128 for col-scale.
+ *  - Output scale_inv size is padded to 128x4 for row-scale and 4x128 for col-scale.
+ *  - MXFP8 inputs may instead use their exact logical scale shapes (M, ceil(K/32))
+ *    rowwise or (ceil(M/32), K) columnwise. Swizzling fills output padding with zeros.
+ *    Other input formats must be padded.
  *  - data is quantized along K-dimension, i.e. 1D-scaling block lies along the K-dimension.
  */
 void nvte_multi_tensor_swizzle_scaling_factors(const NVTETensor* inputs, NVTETensor* outputs,

issue_comments.body:
> I wanted to understand what is the use-case where we have unpadded scales in the mxfp8 tensor?

Sure. Have you seen the issue this PR links to? I've been adding context there because this PR is just for demo at this moment. Shall we follow up over there? 

> TE quantizer always produces padded scales in the MXFP8 Tensor. 

Not really -- according to #3518, quantizer itself works great with unpadded scales. But I could certainly be missing something! 

cc @vthumbe1503

In the issue you mentioned, custom MXFP8Tensor is being created for weight like this.

```
weight = MXFP8Tensor(
    shape=(64, 64),
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device="cuda",
    rowwise_data=empty((64, 64)),
    columnwise_data=empty((64, 64)),
    rowwise_scale_inv=empty((128, 4) if padded else (64, 2)),
    columnwise_scale_inv=empty((4, 128) if padded else (2, 64)),
    fp8_dtype=tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3,
    quantizer=quantizer,
    with_gemm_swizzled_scales=False,
)
```

I see that this is used in Megatron FSDP v2. So I see that you are dealing with weight sharding in FSDP which can be tricky since sharded tensors might not be padded? 


> quantizer itself works great with unpadded scales

I understand quantization works with unpadded scales. So the problem seems to be that GEMMS need swizzled scales padded. 

So 2 solutions can be
1. Pad the compact scales in megatron itself before constructing the MXFP8Tensor shard for the weights. We do something similar in FSD2P. https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/796346c0e0497b1f56a8d36ec76e02db5a6fed47/transformer_engine/pytorch/tensor/mxfp8_tensor.py#L718
2. Or instead of padding and creating a copy for the compact scales.  How about we handle padding directly in the swizzling kernel, to avoid padding performance penalty? We do something similar in grouped swizzling kernel https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/796346c0e0497b1f56a8d36ec76e02db5a6fed47/transformer_engine/common/swizzle/swizzle.cu#L376-L377. Essentially swizzling kernel will be aware that the scales are not padded already. So manually fills them with zeros.


With the current solution, we are silently introducing a performance penalty in the framework by doing the padding, which I am hoping to avoid.

> How about we handle padding directly in the swizzling kernel, to avoid padding performance penalty

I asked my agent to one-shot it. I really don't understand what it's doing. Could you or someone from the TE team take over? @vthumbe1503

reviews.body:
@wujingyue Thanks for the PR!

I wanted to understand what is the use-case where we have unpadded scales in the mxfp8 tensor?

TE quantizer always produces padded scales in the MXFP8 Tensor. And so we should never face this issue where the scales are not padded to (128,4) or (4,128). If external framework is constructing/manipulating the MXFP8Tensor, then I would say, it is the responsibility of that framework and not TE, to pad the scales tensor.

If the external framework cannot sacrifice the performance of additional padding. We can potentially fuse the padding within the swizzling kernel in a way swizzling kernel accepts unpadded scales and fills zero manually in those unpadded locations. We have done something similar for the grouped swizzling kernel.
